title: Integral opposite double flags and their invariant rho boundary
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. Use the rational section modules of [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], with the following explicit description. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend $\rho$ and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. Let $Q=H/B$ denote the scheme representing the fppf sheaf quotient for right multiplication by $B$: this is the sheaf associated to $C\mapsto H(C)/B(C)$, for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. Let $L$ be the homogeneous invertible sheaf [def-sc-invertible-module] on $Q$ associated to the right action $(g,z)b=(gb,\widetilde\rho(b)z)$ on $H\times_A\mathbf A^1_A$. Put $X=Q\times_A Q$ and $D=\operatorname{pr}_1^*L\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*L$. These quotients and associated sheaves exist, $Q$ is smooth and projective over $A$, and $X$ is integral, quasi-compact, separated and flat over $A$ [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Integral means nonempty, irreducible and reduced; flat means flat on local rings. The diagonal $H$-action linearizes $D$. For every $n\ge1$, pullback along $H\to Q$ identifies $\Gamma(Q,L^{\otimes n})$ equivariantly with the actual regular-function module $W_n$ defined above, with its left-translation action. There exist $n_0\in N_H(T)(A)$ representing the Weyl element sending positive roots to negative roots, and an invariant section $d\in\Gamma(X,D)$, such that $B\cap n_0Bn_0^{-1}=T$ and the morphism $q:H\to X$, $g\mapsto(gB,gn_0B)$, factors through $U=X_d$ as a faithfully flat right $T$-torsor. Here $X_d$ is the open where $d$ generates the invertible stalk, and right $T$-torsor means that $q$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation and that $(h,t)\mapsto(h,ht)$ identifies $H\times_A T$ with $H\times_UH$. The open $U$ is dense in $X$ and has nonempty special fibre $U_\kappa$. Pullback gives the equivariant algebra isomorphism $q^*:\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\simeq A[H]^{T,\mathrm{right}}$, where the right side consists of regular functions invariant under right translation after every commutative $A$-algebra extension. The section $d$ and its tensor powers restrict to nowhere vanishing sections on $U$ and on $U_\kappa$. Global sections of the linearized powers of $L,D$ and of $\mathcal O_U$ carry the induced rational $H$-coactions, restriction maps commute with these coactions, and $d$ is invariant as a coaction identity. For the trivial group these assertions mean $Q=X=U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $L=D=\mathcal O$, and $d=1$.

source.place: Section 9.7, construction before Lemma 9.7.2 and Property I(b), printed pp.526--527. Agent-formulated integral double-flag supporting lemma, not a verbatim theorem of Alper. Field geometry read in Milne, Algebraic Groups, Theorems 21.80 and 21.84 and Remark 22.49, pp.450--451,479--480; integral version WANTED: Seshadri, Geometric reductivity over arbitrary base, Property I and its proof, p.247. No SGA route is used.

proof.text: A DVR is a local PID, so it is Noetherian. The hypotheses on the geometric fibres of H imply reductivity: a connected normal unipotent subgroup is solvable and hence is trivial. Apply the local Borel quotient geometry to obtain B=T⋉V, the projection B→T, a smooth proper scheme Q representing H/B, and the faithfully flat quasi-compact locally finitely presented B-torsor π:H→Q. Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. These are the quotient and radical required in the statement, with the same positive-root convention.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.8 and Theorem 5.2.11; Noetherianity: Stacks Tag 00FM

proof.text: On the fpqc cover π, put the trivial line with descent multiplier ρ̃(b) on (g,gb). Multiplicativity of ρ̃ is exactly the cocycle condition, so fpqc descent gives an invertible sheaf L with the stated associated-bundle description. Left multiplication on H commutes with right B multiplication and leaves the multiplier unchanged; its maps therefore descend to a linearization. The same construction gives its powers and D. A section of L^n pulls back to a regular function f on H whose compatibility on H×_QH=H×B is f(gb)=ρ̃(b)^n f(g); conversely precisely this identity descends f uniquely. Thus Γ(Q,L^n)=W_n. Left translation on these functions is (h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g), so the identification is equivariant.

source.place: Descent, Tags 023T and 03DT; associated line with positive multiplier

proof.text: On every geometric A-fibre, the coroot pairings of ρ with the simple roots are 1. The strictly dominant flag-line lemma applies to the line constructed in step 2 (its multiplier is +ρ, namely the convention M_ρ of that lemma), and shows that this fibre line is ample. The relative ample-locus theorem applied to the proper scheme Q/A therefore has every point of Spec A in its open locus, so L is relatively ample on all of Q. The proper-relative-ample theorem makes Q projective in the projective-bundle sense. The ambient finite-type quasi-coherent module on Spec A has finitely many generators, giving a degreewise surjection A[T_0,...,T_N]→Sym(E). The relative-Proj functoriality theorem makes P(E)→P^N_A a closed immersion. Composing the two closed immersions gives projectivity also in the finite-projective-space convention.

source.place: Tags 0D3D and 0BCL; fibre line: Milne positive-root convention, sign audited against M_ρ

proof.text: The projections Q×_A Q→Q are smooth and proper by base change, and their composites to Spec A are smooth and proper. Thus X is quasi-compact and separated, and it is flat by the smoothness criterion. It is Noetherian because it is of finite type over the Noetherian ring A. Let E be an algebraic closure of the fraction field of A. The field double-flag lemma says X_E is integral. For any nonempty affine open Spec R⊂X, the affine flatness criterion and flat-implies-torsionfree lemma make R torsion-free over A. Thus localization at the nonzero elements followed by the faithful field extension embeds R into R⊗_A E; the latter is the ring of a nonempty affine open of X_E, hence a domain. Thus each such R is a domain. Moreover every nonempty open of X meets its generic fibre, by the same injection on an affine subopen. The generic fibre is irreducible, since its surjective base change X_E is irreducible. Any two nonempty opens of X therefore intersect. X is nonempty (it contains (B,B)), irreducible and reduced, hence integral.

source.place: Tags 01W4, 01VB, 01V8, 01VF, 01T6; generic-fibre integrality from the cited field version

proof.text: Take the relative root subgroups and Weyl representatives for (H,T). Use the positive system occurring in B; it is the same on every geometric fibre by step 1. A functional taking value 1 on its simple roots is positive on its positive roots; extend it rationally to the character space and clear denominators to obtain the integer functional required by the root-product theorem. The positive-root product gives B_+=T⋉V_+ with these roots. At the closed fibre B_+ and B have the same nonzero tangent weights. The Borel case of local parabolic Lie comparison therefore identifies B_+=B, and hence V_+=V. The unique Weyl element w_0 reversing positives has a representative n_0∈N_H(T)(A). Root conjugation identifies n_0Bn_0^{-1} with T⋉V_- by applying the root products. Use the relative open-cell theorem also for the reversed positive system. It gives the open immersion V×T×V_-→H and hence, after right translation by n_0, V×B→H, (u,b)↦un_0b. Denote its image C. In every geometric fibre C is the dense longest Bruhat cell.

The relative root coordinates also prove B∩n_0Bn_0^{-1}=T scheme-theoretically. Indeed for every test algebra, an equality ut=t'v with u∈V and v∈V_- gives equal coordinates (u,t,1)=(1,t',v) in the open immersion V×T×V_-→H. Therefore u=v=1 and t=t'. This gives equality of the subgroup functors, including nonreduced test algebras. The B-stable open C⊂H is saturated for π since its coordinates are V×B. Its two pullbacks to H×_QH agree. Fpqc descent of opens therefore gives C_Q⊂Q with π^{-1}(C_Q)=C. Taking the quotient of V×B by its second factor identifies C_Q≅V, via u↦un_0B. For the inverse: V≅A^N_A is affine by the root-product coordinates of step 5, and the N coordinate functions of the first factor of C≅V×B are B-invariant, so their two pullbacks to C×_{C_Q}C=C×B agree; descent of sections of O along the fpqc cover π|_C:C→C_Q gives the inverse morphism C_Q→V.

source.place: Tags 03N0 and 03DT; the subgroup equality follows directly from the coordinates of step 5

proof.text: Apply the integral primitive-normalization lemma for m=1 with the open cell and representative of step 5. Obtain f∈W_1 with f(n_0)=1 and f(bg)=ρ̃(b)^{-1}f(g) on all test algebras. We claim D(f)=C as open subschemes of H. Check on each algebraically closed A-field F. In the Bruhat chart u n_w b, the two transformation laws give f(u n_w b)=ρ̃(b)f(n_w). For t∈T(F), evaluating t n_w=n_w(n_w^{-1}tn_w) gives ρ(t)^{-1}f(n_w)=(wρ)(t)f(n_w). Distinct characters of a split torus over the infinite field F are distinct functions on its points. Consequently f(n_w)≠0 forces wρ=-ρ, hence w=w_0. On the longest chart f(n_0)=1, so the function never vanishes. The finite Bruhat stratification covers H_F, proving D(f)_F=C_F. Equality on all geometric points of H proves equality of the two relative opens.

source.place: Theorem 21.80 and Proposition 22.22; integral normalization separated as its own supporting lemma

proof.text: On H×_A H define δ(g,h)=f(g^{-1}h). Its transformation under (b_1,b_2) is δ(gb_1,hb_2)=ρ̃(b_1)ρ̃(b_2)δ(g,h), an identity after every A-algebra extension. Thus δ is a compatible section for the descent datum of D, and fpqc section descent along π×π gives d∈Γ(X,D). The identity δ(sg,sh)=δ(g,h) gives invariance of this section under the diagonal action, including arbitrary test algebras. In particular δ(1,n_0)=1, so d is nonzero and its nonvanishing open U has a point (B,n_0B) over A and over κ. Since X is integral, this nonempty open is dense.

source.place: Tag 03DT; direct regular-function construction motivated by Alper §9.7, printed p.526

proof.text: Pull U→Q (the first projection) back along the fpqc cover H→Q. A point there is (a,y) with the coefficient of d at (aB,y) nonzero. Translation by a^{-1} identifies the permitted y with C_Q, by D(f)=C, so this pullback is H×V, with y=a u n_0B. It has the section g=a u of the pullback of q. For two elements g,g' giving the same pair, g^{-1}g' belongs both to B and to n_0Bn_0^{-1}, hence uniquely to T by step 6. Accordingly the pullback of q over H×V is explicitly (H×V)×T→H×V, with g=a u t. These formulas are inverse on all test schemes and prove H×T≅H×_UH. The projection is flat, surjective and finitely presented: T is a split torus, its Laurent coordinate algebra is a free faithfully flat finitely presented algebra. Flatness and local finite presentation descend along the fpqc cover; the local sections prove surjectivity. Hence q:H→U is the asserted fppf right T-torsor.

source.place: Tags 02L2 and 02KY; explicit trivialization by the opposite-cell coordinates

proof.text: Apply the affine-torsor-invariants theorem with base A, affine total space H, flat affine structure group T, quotient U and algebra O_U. It identifies q^*:Γ(U,O_U) with A[H]^{T,right}; its fixed elements are the full coaction equalizer, equivalently right invariance after every A-algebra extension. Since q(sg)=s q(g), pullback commutes with left translation. Thus this algebra isomorphism is H-equivariant once global sections are supplied the coactions constructed in the next step.

source.place: Descent on Spaces Tag 04W8 and Schemes Tag 01IB, as in the cited affine-torsor theorem

proof.text: For Y=Q,X,U and a linearized power F of L,D, or F=O_U, let R=A[H]. The scheme Y is quasi-compact and separated: Q,X are proper of finite type, and U is an open in the Noetherian X. Since H is smooth, R is A-flat. Degree-zero flat base change for the quasi-coherent sheaf F identifies Γ(Y×_A H,pr_Y^*F)=Γ(Y,F)⊗_A R. Pull a section back by (y,h)↦h^{-1}y and use the linearization to obtain the coaction c on Γ(Y,F). The identity and product action laws give (1⊗ε)c=id and (c⊗1)c=(1⊗Δ)c: the same base-change isomorphism applies again with H×H, so these equalities of pulled-back sections are equalities in the stated tensor modules. Restriction to an invariant open and tensor powers commute with these pullbacks. In particular all restriction maps in the statement commute with coactions, and δ(sg,sh)=δ(g,h) from step 8 descends to c(d)=d⊗1. This also proves that the section-module identification in step 2 and the function-algebra identification in step 10 are identities of rational H-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes flat base change, Tags 02KH and 02KE; apply to the actual quasi-coherent line, not just the structure sheaf

proof.text: By definition of X_d, d trivializes D on U. Therefore d^n trivializes D^n there for each n≥1, and pulling this trivialization to κ proves the corresponding assertion on U_κ. If H is the trivial group, B=T=H, Q=X=Spec A, V is the empty product, ρ is trivial and the normalized function in step 7 is f=1. All the displayed constructions then give U=Spec A, L=D=O and d=1.
